This PR introduces a formalization of the bijective base-2 numeration system. Unlike standard binary representation, bijective base-2 avoids the "leading zeros" problem, providing a strict mathematical bijection between natural numbers (ℕ) and lists of booleans (List Bool). All CI checks are passing. Since I am a new contributor, I would greatly appreciate it if a maintainer could take a look or add the appropriate labels to put it in the review queue.

Thanks!
Out of curiosity, is there interesting math theorem related to this?

Weiyi Wang

The main motivation is to provide a canonical, strictly bijective encoding between ℕ and finite boolean strings.

This strict bijection is highly useful for example in
Algorithmic Information Theory (Kolmogorov Complexity):
To formally define the complexity of a natural number K(n),
you need to map it uniquely to a bitstring.
Huh do we not already have this?
#35857
Like I see your thinking with bijectivity and that but I think having this as well as docs#Nat.bits and docs#Nat.ofBits would be bad.
ultimately you're kind of I think proposing a variant on Nat.bits that doesn't use binaryRec but maybe one of its variants
We also already have docs#Nat.digits and docs#Nat.ofDigits

We also have docs#Num which I think more directly corresponds to this representation of Nat. I'm not sure why we don't have docs#Num.ofNat, we only have docs#Num.ofNat'. But you see the issue: this is ultimately not a new contribution.
And it doesn't really use any of the existing constructions

Now don't get me wrong - I think it's not great that we have so many similar things already but don't quite have the thing you suggest. There's no reason I think why Nat.ofBits couldn't take a list instead and if it did I think it would more or less be your suggestion. I also think Nat.bit is a pretty useful function we should consider backporting. The issue is that adding yet another binary representation of Nat is, unfortunately, I fear the opposite of a helpful contribution.
The thing is I think having the bijection is cool! But it comes at the cost of the bijection not really making good sense with respect to other representations.

Wrenna Robson

Thanks for the comments! To be honest, I'm not entirely sure what you are suggesting as a next step.

As you noted, having a strict bijection is cool. We currently don't have one in Mathlib, and sooner or later, this (or something very similar) will need to be implemented as a foundational tool for Kolmogorov complexity (which is my main motivation) or combinatorics on words.

Because of this, I'm trying to understand what exactly the issue is with my implementation from your perspective. Would it help to move this code into the Computability folder/namespace so it doesn't cause confusion with standard binary arithmetic representations, or do you have a different approach in mind?

Wrenna Robson

Just to add a quick point regarding the bijection:

While Mathlib technically has abstract bijections between ℕ and List Bool (e.g., via Denumerable), for many applications we specifically need a length-lexicographic bijection.

The crucial property we need is that the length of the mapped string must be roughly equal to the base-2 logarithm of the number (i.e., length $\approx \log_2 n$). The current generic bijections in Mathlib do not preserve this length bound at all, but this logarithmic bound is strictly required for Kolmogorov complexity and bounding program sizes.
Yeah I think there's absolutely a case for providing a better concrete bijection. But I think that bound is true of Nat.bits?

Wrenna Robson
Thanks for the discussion! It actually led me to re-evaluate the formalization requirements, and I want to share three thoughts to clarify the situation:

  1. The mathematical gap is real: Mathematically, Mathlib currently lacks a bijection ℕ ≃ List Bool that also satisfies the logarithmic length bound. Existing Denumerable instances do not preserve lengths, and Nat.bits is not a bijection (it is not surjective onto List Bool because it cannot output strings with "leading/trailing" zeros).

  2. The AIT formalization insight: However, for Kolmogorov Complexity specifically, I realized that I don't actually need a strict bijection. Textbooks (like Li & Vitányi) use a bijection purely for pedagogical convenience to freely swap numbers and strings. In a strict formalization, any total computable injection (like Nat.bits) is sufficient because the Invariance Theorem ($O(1)$ constant) absorbs the translation overhead. The pushback from the library's architecture helped me separate textbook "sugar" from formal necessity, which is a very interesting takeaway!

Following up on the discussion here: I decided to pivot away from the bijective base-2 implementation. Instead, I've addressed the gap mentioned by @Wrenna Robson regarding Nat.ofBits and lists.

I've opened PR #36463, which introduces Nat.ofBitsList (a version of ofBits taking a List Bool, named to avoid collision with Batteries) and proves Nat.bits_injective using it. This provides the missing inverse for the existing Nat.bits API without introducing a new numeration system.

This looks great - I would probably make this an abbrev rather than a def and I'm not sure about the name but I like it. There's probably a theorem about bits_ofBitsList - certainly if the last entry is true I think this holds (which is maybe some kind of InjOn statement?)
I am going to have a tinker and probably suggest some changes and additions. I can't push to your PR directly though. I might push a PR to your branch if you like or I can just add comments.
I ended up with a lot of changes to the file that I think would be good - honestly I think it's a little bit of a mess currently. Some of that will help with your one.
Sounds great! Please feel free to open a PR against my branch. Looking forward to seeing your changes.

Hi @Wrenna Robson and @Jon Eugster,

Following up on PR #36463. Jon suggested in his review that it might be better to upstream this to Batteries rather than patching the legacy Bits.lean file in Mathlib.

Wrenna, since you mentioned earlier that you were looking into refactoring this file, I just wanted to check in. I'm available to do the work myself if you haven't started yet — either refactoring it here in Mathlib or opening a PR to Batteries.

How should we proceed?
Sorry I was quite busy with some life stuff

I suggest before you actually create the PR itself we discuss the form it should take - maybe a new thread would be appropriate for that?
I would quite like to do some of the work myself and it might be that it's better to make this a sequence of PRs.
I think we should look at deprecating the Mathlib stuff also eventually.
